analysis.title: Market Update US, Europe & Asia (6 November 2026)
key_insights: US equities fell sharply on Thursday near the lows. The S&P 500 fell 4.36%, the Nasdaq 5.52% and the Dow 3.44%, more than erasing Wednesday's post-election gains. The S&P 500, Nasdaq and Russell 2000 all had their worst sessions since April 2025.

The AI trade was the main drag. Double-digit declines were widespread across semiconductors, semicap, memory and neoclouds, and the SOX had its worst day since March 2020. TSLA and NVDA were the notable Mag 7 decliners.

The report ties the risk-off move to capacity concerns coming out of the midterms, with no cushion from the broadening-out trade. The equal-weight S&P held up nearly 150 bp better than the cap-weighted index.

The market has been unable to take advantage of strong earnings growth (Q3 running at nearly +32%). The report attributes this to scrutiny of peak growth and peak capex dynamics and a potentially slower AI buildout.
Treasuries were firmer and the curve flattened, with short-end yields down 10-11 bp. The dollar index was flat and gold rose about 1%.

WTI crude rose 2.7% on Thursday but is sharply lower on the week after a 15%+ three-day drop on diplomatic hopes. WTI futures do not see crude back below $80/barrel until June. Hormuz incidents continue, and higher energy flows through the strait depend on an extensive military deployment.
Initial jobless claims were 189K vs 196K consensus, the lowest since 1969. Continuing claims were 1718K vs 1719K consensus. Preliminary Q3 productivity of 3.6% SAAR beat the 2.8% consensus.

The October Challenger report showed job cuts down 71% y/y to the lowest October level since 2023. AI-related cuts fell to a 2026 low of 1,265 but are about 20% of YTD layoffs. Planned hiring rose 57% y/y.

October nonfarm payrolls are due Friday at 8:30 ET. Consensus is +65K (September +29K), private payrolls +65K and unemployment 4.2%. Previews flag headwinds from a UAW strike and the revocation of Haitian TPS status, and upside from construction, manufacturing and leisure/hospitality. The print is seen as unlikely to move the Fed much.

Fed speakers stayed hawkish. Cleveland's Hammack (voter) expects policy to need to become more restrictive and prefers frequent, smaller adjustments. Richmond's Barkin (non-voter) sees rates rising further but says policy is close to neutral.

Earnings reactions were large and mixed. APP rose 31% on a Q3 beat and a $3.2B larger buyback. VCYT fell 54.3% on a guidance cut. QCOM fell 9.5% on handsets, ARM 13.1% on smartphone royalties and EXPE 13.7% on a weak Q4 guide.

European equities finished mostly lower after giving up gains late in the session as the US selloff deepened. The Stoxx 600 is close to August's record closing high. Tech, industrials and telecom lagged, while chemicals, retail and defensives led.

The BoE raised its key rate 25 bp to 4% in an 8-1 vote. Mann backed 50 bp. Its projection has inflation peaking at 4.9% in Q2 2027 and back at target by late 2028. A December follow-up hike is not certain because Breeden, Ramsden and Lombardelli flagged downside inflation risks.
Norges Bank held at 4.50% and said it is prepared to raise rates if warranted. SEB, Nordea and DNB see 4.50% as the probable peak, with cuts not expected until late 2027.
EU leaders aim to appoint Lagarde's successor at the mid-December summit. The Dutch government nominated Knot, Spain is expected to nominate de Cos, and Germany's Nagel is reportedly keen.
Eurozone data: PPI surprised to the upside, German September factory orders rose 4.4% m/m vs 4.8% expected, and the UK construction PMI fell to 43.6 vs 46.1 consensus.

Asian equities were volatile and mixed. Memory and chip names fell on AI-buildout worries: Kioxia -13%, SK Hynix -9.5% and Samsung -7.6%, taking the Taiex to a three-month low. Hong Kong rose 3.67% on a rotation into IT and consumer stocks, and India rose 2.40% and is up 6.0% on the week.
China blocked SoftBank's $5.4B purchase of ABB's robotics unit, and SoftBank fell 6.8%. YMTC paused its IPO. Toyota rose 16.7% after raising its FY profit forecast by 15%.

The September BOJ minutes showed support for continued rate hikes. Bank Negara Malaysia held at 2.75% but still omitted 'appropriate' from its commentary, which the report reads as keeping room to hike.

market_movers.rationale: Stock +31% on a Q3 revenue and margin beat, Q4 guidance well above the Street and a $3.2B larger buyback.
Stock -54.3% after cutting FY26 guidance. Decipher volumes disappointed and the initial 2027 growth outlook of mid-single digits is well below the Street.
Stock -9.5%. Handsets missed on a declining iPhone and Q4 EPS was guided below, while data center, auto, IoT and AI accelerators were cited as offsets.
Stock -13.1% on continued royalty pressure from weak smartphones and valuation scrutiny, despite an in-line to better Q3 guide.
Stock -13.7% on a weak Q4 guide on softer travel demand, though Q3 bookings, revenue and EBITDA beat.
Stock -13% despite better FQ1 results and guidance ahead of the Street. It expects FY27 pro forma revenue growth of 60%+, and analysts are watching for commitments to turn into cash flow.
BTIG downgraded to neutral from buy, citing a high bar and recurring revenue growth that decelerated from Q2, after a Q3 beat and raised guidance. Stock -6.8%.
Stock -12.1% on a Q3 EBIT miss from investment, shipping, fuel and fulfillment costs, with slower Mexico flagged.
Stock -9.4% on Q3 revenue and EBITDA misses and below-consensus Q4 guidance, with housing demand headwinds from higher mortgage rates.
Stock -16.7% despite Q3 beats and raised FY26 revenue guidance, as analysts were cautious on growth durability and disappointed by billings and RPO.
Stock -21.4% after lowering FY26 revenue, EBITDA and comp guidance, with slowing traffic and competition concerns.
Stock -14% as revenue and DAUs missed and core ad growth slowed, despite an EPS and EBITDA beat and Q4 guidance ahead of expectations.
Stock -14.2%. Q3 organic growth of +3.3% missed by over 400 bp, partly offset by an EPS beat that the tariff refund helped.
Stock -17.1% after lowering FY26 Galleri revenue growth guidance on disappointing volumes and price.
Stock -7.4% as the FQ3 outlook calls for 3-4% growth after FQ2 constant-currency growth of 10%.
Stock +7.1% on fiscal Q1 sales, margins and EPS ahead, raised FY guidance and capital return of about $2B in FY27.
Stock +12.3% on a sharp Q3 EPS and revenue beat, though FY26 cash generation guidance was cut again.
Stock +22.5% on Q3 revenue, gross margin and EBITDA ahead and a raised low end of FY26 revenue guidance.
Stock +30.7% on Q3 EPS and revenue beats and raised FY26 revenue guidance.
Stock +1.8% as October US comps ex-gas accelerated to +8.1%, better than expected.
Fiscal 2027 outlook (comparable revenue growth of 4-5%, adjusted EPS of €2.20-2.40) was viewed as insufficient to justify the valuation.
An analyst keeps an Underperform stance despite a 17% quarterly profit beat, citing declining reinsurance revenue and premium valuations.
Analysts reiterated Outperform after a revenue and gross profit beat and a slight EBITA miss.

earnings_insights: APP: Q3 earnings, revenue and margins beat (reported), Q4 guidance well above the Street, and the buyback was increased by $3.2B. Stock +31%.
QCOM: fiscal Q4 revenue and EPS better than expected (reported), Handsets missed on a declining iPhone, and Q4 EPS was guided below. Stock -9.5%.
ARM: fiscal Q2 ahead (reported), Q3 guide in line to better, and royalties are under pressure from weak smartphones. Stock -13.1%.
EXPE: Q3 bookings, revenue and EBITDA better (reported), Q4 guide weak on softer travel demand. Stock -13.7%.
VCYT: Q3 beat (reported), Decipher volumes disappointed, FY26 revenue and testing sales guidance lowered, and 2027 growth outlook of mid-single digits well below the Street. Stock -54.3%.
COHR: FQ1 earnings and revenue better (reported), next-Q guidance ahead of the Street, FY27 pro forma revenue growth of 60%+ expected, and a ~$20B PhotonLink agreement starting in 2028. Stock -13%.
SNAP: Q3 EPS and EBITDA beat (reported) but revenue and DAUs missed. Q4 guidance was ahead of expectations. Stock -14%.
FIG: Q3 net income, EPS, revenue and FCF all beat (reported), FY26 revenue guidance raised, and billings and RPO disappointing. Stock -16.7%.
BROS: Q3 EPS, revenue and EBITDA beat (reported), comps slightly missed, and FY26 revenue, EBITDA and comp guidance was lowered. Stock -21.4%.

ROK: Q3 organic growth of +3.3% missed by over 400 bp (reported), though it was largely in line excluding the tariff refund. EPS beat with help from the tariff refund. ARR growth slowed to +5% from +6%. Stock -14.2%.
MELI: Q3 EBIT missed (reported) on weaker margins. Stock -12.1%.
ZG: Q3 revenue and EBITDA missed (reported), and Q4 revenue and EBITDA were guided below. Stock -9.4%.
RL: FQ2 EPS and revenue beat (reported) with constant-currency sales growth of 10% vs guidance of 5-6%. FQ3 outlook is 3-4% growth. Stock -7.4%.
PAYC: Q3 EPS, EBITDA and revenue all beat (reported), and FY26 revenue, EBITDA and ARR guidance was raised. Stock -6.8% on a BTIG downgrade.
TPR: fiscal Q1 sales, margins and EPS ahead (reported), raised FY guidance, and capital return boosted to about $2B in FY27. Stock +7.1%.
DNUT: Q3 EPS and revenue beat (reported), EBITDA slightly missed, and FY26 revenue guidance was raised. Stock +30.7%.
WRBY: Q3 revenue, gross margin and EBITDA ahead (reported), low end of FY26 revenue guidance raised. Stock +22.5%.
RUN: Q3 EPS and revenue sharply beat (reported), and FY26 cash generation guidance was cut again. Stock +12.3%.
CAVA: Q3 EPS, revenue, EBITDA and comps missed (reported), with about a 150 bp Cyclospora headwind. FY26 comp guidance was raised and the EBITDA outlook narrowed below consensus. Stock -3.2%.
FOUR: Q3 adjusted EBITDA better but net revenue missed (reported). Q4 guidance was below consensus and FY EPS guidance was cut. Stock -4.5%.
CMI: Q3 earnings better but revenue and EBITDA margin missed (reported), and the FY revenue-growth guidance midpoint was lowered. Stock -4.9%.

Maersk Q3 (reported): underlying EBITDA of $4.72B vs $5.28B consensus, revenue of $18.10B vs $18.25B consensus, and underlying net income of $3.03B vs $3.54B consensus. FY EBITDA guidance was raised to $14-14.5B from $10.5-12.5B, the third upgrade of the year.

Rheinmetall: FY sales guidance cut for the second time in three months to about €13.2B from €13.7-14.2B, below the lowest analyst estimate, and the operating margin target was cut to about 18.5% from about 19%. Q3 sales were €3.15B (reported). Stock -16.1%.
Nemetschek Q3 (reported): adjusted EPS of €0.66 vs €0.45 consensus, revenue of €371.1M in line, and EBITDA of €115.9M vs €115.1M consensus. Manage segment guidance was cut and the stock fell 9.7%.

Commerzbank Q3 (reported): net income of €859M vs €864M consensus, revenue of €3.20B and operating profit of €1.31B slightly missed. NII guidance was trimmed to about €8.5B from about €8.6B. Stock -2.4%.
HelloFresh Q3 (reported): revenue of €1.4B was 1% ahead of consensus and adjusted EBITDA of €50.9M was 11% ahead. Stock +13%.
Toyota (reported Q2): revenue and operating income ahead of estimates, FY profit forecast raised 15%. Stock +16.7%.
Astellas (reported Q2): core net income of ¥161.0B vs ¥141.16B estimate, and FY guidance was raised. Stock +6.9%.
Autohome (reported Q3): non-GAAP EPADS of CNY2.42 vs CNY2.02 estimate. Stock +8.6%.

risk_factors: Capacity concerns and a potentially slower AI buildout, with scrutiny on peak growth and peak capex.
A lingering lack of a credible near-term diplomatic offramp on the Iran war, and renewed oil strength.
Hawkish Fed speakers (Hammack, Barkin) backing rate hikes.
Hidden risks in intermediaries helping finance the AI buildout (Barkin).
Housing demand headwinds from higher mortgage rates (Zillow).
Memory chip supply crisis affecting European industrials (Kontron).
Delay of Rheinmetall's Arminius Boxer contract award to 2027.
US-China tension affecting deals, with China blocking SoftBank's purchase of ABB's robotics unit.
vol_and_positioning: Volatility index rose 69.66% on the day to 28.18, with a 45.11% gain month to date.
The equal-weight S&P held up nearly 150 bp better than the cap-weighted index, and breadth was negative.
The report says there was no cushion from the broadening-out trade, which had been rotating money rather than de-risking until now.
geopolitical: Iran war and Mideast diplomacy: WTI fell 15%+ in three days on hopes that Trump could seek a post-election settlement. The report notes the analysis is largely speculation. VP Vance said the war was a major factor in the midterm result, and Axios discussed Trump's choice between renewed kinetic action and negotiation.
Strait of Hormuz incidents continue (Reuters), and higher energy flows depend on an extensive, expensive military deployment.
US midterm elections: Democrats promise more scrutiny of White House efforts to wind back emission rules and may try to revive solar and wind subsidies.
China blocked SoftBank's $5.4B purchase of ABB's robotics unit.
The Eurozone ECB presidency race: EU leaders aim to appoint Lagarde's successor at the mid-December summit, with Knot, de Cos and Nagel mentioned.
cross_bank_references: BTIG downgraded PAYC to neutral from buy.
Analysts are described as broadly positive on COHR but watching when commitments turn into cash flow.
